name: Government Complex Sejong
key_features: Fifteen low ministry buildings joined by one winding roof garden about 3.6 km long.

name: Seonyudo Park
by: Seoahn Total Landscape (Jung Young-sun), Joh Sung-yong
key_features: A former water-treatment plant on a Han River island, its concrete tanks and columns kept as gardens.

name: Seoul National University Museum of Art
key_features: A box cut to follow the hillside and lifted on one central core, so the ground beneath stays an open path.

name: Galileo Galilei Planetarium
key_features: Sphere-like concrete form round a 20 m domed projection hall with 360 seats, on its own in Palermo's parks.

name: Serra Dourada Stadium
key_features: Exposed-concrete stadium bowl; look at the structural rhythm and the long access ramps.

name: National Art Schools (Escuelas Nacionales de Arte)
by: Ricardo Porro, Vittorio Garatti, Roberto Gottardi
key_features: Five schools of local brick and Catalan tile vaults on a former golf course; Porro's art school is a village of domes.

name: Jaú Bus Station
key_features: Bus station under one concrete roof carried on columns that branch out round skylights; ramps link the levels.

name: Forma Furniture Showroom
key_features: A closed prism lifted on two 30 m beams over street parking; one full-width shop window faces the avenue.

name: Sheikh Zayed Bridge
key_features: Sweeping steel arches that rise and fall along the road deck as it crosses the channel to Abu Dhabi island.

name: Lusail Stadium
key_features: Host stadium of the 2022 World Cup final, designed by Foster + Partners with Populous.

name: Qatar University
key_features: Precast octagonal modules on a grid, each classroom topped by a wind tower for cool air and soft daylight.

name: King Khalid International Airport
key_features: Triangular terminals, and a Royal Terminal whose roof of 33 arched sections rises 30 m.

name: Maraya
key_features: A concert hall wrapped in 9,740 m2 of mirror, a box that reflects the desert canyon until it nearly disappears.

name: Holiday Inn Beirut
key_features: A 26-storey hotel open only a year before the civil war; its gutted frame still stands as a war memory.

name: Monument to the Unknown Soldier (1959)
key_features: Chadirji turned the brick arch of Ctesiphon into a thin concrete arch in Firdos Square.

name: Federation of Industries Building
key_features: One of Chadirji's brick office buildings, his search for a modern architecture rooted in Iraq.

name: Izvestia Building
key_features: Constructivist newspaper office: a grid of big windows topped by a row of round ones.

name: Sarpi Border Checkpoint
key_features: White tower of cantilevered viewing terraces marking the Georgia-Turkey border by the Black Sea.

name: Hotel Kazakhstan
by: Yuri Ratushny, Leonid Ukhobotov, Vladimir Kim
key_features: Tall slab hotel with a crown-like top, built to stand up to Almaty's earthquakes.

name: Kazakhstan Central Concert Hall
key_features: Curving blue glass 'petals' wrap the concert hall like an opening flower.

name: Flying Saucer (UkrINTEI)
key_features: Saucer-shaped hall hovering over a long low glazed base on a narrow street site.

name: Salyut Hotel
key_features: Round hotel whose floors hang around a concrete core; its planned height was cut by more than half.

name: Palace of the Republic
by: Nikolai Ripinsky, Leonid Ukhobotov and team
key_features: Concert palace under a deep overhanging roof above a glazed front.

name: Tallinn Song Festival Stage
by: Alar Kotli, Henno Sepmann, Uno Tölpus
key_features: Great arched shell over tiers for thousands of singers, facing a grassy natural amphitheatre.

name: Zvartnots Airport Old Terminal
by: Artur Tarkhanyan, Spartak Khachikyan, Levon Cherkezyan, Zhorzh Shekhlyan
key_features: Round terminal ringed by gates, with the control tower rising from the centre of the circle.

name: Queen Tamar Airport
key_features: Tiny mountain terminal: a white sculptural tower of cut-out shapes beside a small hall.

name: Central Research Institute of Robotics and Technical Cybernetics
key_features: Concrete research tower shaped like a rocket on its launch pad, built to test space robotics.

name: Lascaux IV
key_features: A long low building cut into the hillside like a fault line, where visitors walk into a replica of the cave.

name: Fondation Avicenne (Maison de l'Iran)
by: Claude Parent, André Bloc, Mohsen Foroughi, Heydar Ghiai
key_features: Student rooms in blocks hung from giant steel portal frames, lifted clear of the ground.

name: Fondation Jérôme Seydoux-Pathé
key_features: A curved shell of perforated aluminium rising in a courtyard behind a facade carved by Rodin.

name: Teatro Regio
key_features: Mollino's brick-walled opera house behind the old 18th-century facade, with a shell-shaped hall inside.

name: Museo Enzo Ferrari
key_features: A yellow aluminium roof, shaped like a car bonnet with air-intake slots, curls round Enzo Ferrari's birthplace.

name: Erdene Zuu Monastery
key_features: A square walled compound ringed by 108 stupas, built from the stones of Karakorum.

name: Kauchuk Factory Club
key_features: Constructivist workers' club whose curved auditorium front faces the street.

name: Kyiv Crematorium (Park of Memory)
by: Avraham Miletsky, Ada Rybachuk, Volodymyr Melnychenko
key_features: Farewell halls as swelling white concrete forms set into the hillside of Baikove cemetery.

name: Tbilisi Public Service Hall
key_features: Giant white petal-like roofs on stems shelter a cluster of glass office blocks by the river.

name: Hotel Uzbekistan
key_features: Curved slab whose whole face is a lattice of concrete sun-screens in an eastern pattern.

name: Kuwait Water Towers
key_features: Groups of 'mushroom' towers: a slim concrete stem under a broad conical tank, repeated across the city.

name: Šerefudin's White Mosque
key_features: All-white mosque whose roof is a freely deformed quarter-dome pierced by five skylights; tubular minaret.

name: Universiti Teknologi Petronas
key_features: Five crescent-shaped buildings around a landscaped centre, linked by vast curved canopies that shade the walkways.

name: Hassan II Bridge
key_features: Three parallel decks, two for road and one for tram, each carried on low concrete arches across the Bou Regreg.

name: Madinat al-Zahra Museum
key_features: Museum set low into the ground like an excavation: a sequence of courtyards walled in pale concrete.

name: Majara Residence
key_features: About 200 superadobe domes in bright colours, clustered like a village by the sea, with paths between them.

name: Central Market, Koudougou
key_features: Market of compressed earth blocks built as vaults, domes and arches, with a covered hall of 624 stalls.

name: Jahad Metro Plaza
key_features: Metro entrance rebuilt as linked brick arches and vaults, about 300,000 handmade bricks, around a pedestrian plaza.

name: Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India
key_features: Brick campus of seven or eight blocks along two axes around courtyards, with deep arcades for the heat.

name: Price Tower
key_features: Wright's only built skyscraper: floors cantilever like branches from a central core, with copper louvres.

name: Sainsbury Wing, National Gallery
key_features: Portland stone front borrows the old gallery's pilasters, then thins them out; top-lit galleries recall Soane.

name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
key_features: Built on the Hovden sardine cannery site, keeping its boiler-house smokestacks; decks and tanks open onto the bay.

name: The Box (Conjunctive Points)
key_features: A skewed box-shaped room perches on an old warehouse roof: part of Moss's remaking of the Hayden Tract.

name: Washington Metro stations
key_features: One idea repeated underground: a coffered concrete vault lit indirectly from below, with no columns on the platform.

name: Florey Building
key_features: Student rooms in a red-tiled horseshoe that leans back on raking concrete legs, opening to the River Cherwell.

name: Santa Maria Church, Marco de Canaveses
key_features: A tall white box: two towers frame a 10 m door, and a long low window lets the nave look out at sitting height.

name: Palais des Expositions (Grand Palais), Charleroi
by: AgwA, architecten jan de vylder inge vinck
key_features: 1950s exhibition halls kept and opened up: facades taken off so the central hall becomes a covered public foyer.

name: Stadthaus Scharnhauser Park
key_features: Town hall whose upper floors overhang the square as a deep canopy, with a field of light rods in front.

name: NAVEZ, 5 social housing units
key_features: Five social flats for large families in a slim corner block at the northern entrance to Brussels.

name: Zénith de Strasbourg
key_features: Concert hall wrapped in orange textile membrane over elliptical steel rings that twist as they rise.

name: Rivesaltes Camp Memorial
key_features: Long concrete monolith sunk into the old camp, its roof no higher than the ruined barracks around it.

name: Katyń Museum
key_features: Museum in a 19th-century citadel fort; a narrow stair cuts straight through the earth rampart.

name: Saw Swee Hock Student Centre, LSE
key_features: Faceted brick block shaped by the narrow streets around it, with perforated brick screens over its windows.

name: Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision
key_features: Cube of coloured glass printed with TV images in relief; half the building, the archive, is sunk below ground.

name: Groot Klimmendaal Rehabilitation Centre
key_features: Rehabilitation centre in woodland: long dark volumes stacked and cantilevered over the slope, full of daylight.

name: PLATO Contemporary Art Gallery
key_features: Old municipal slaughterhouse turned art gallery; new concrete panels fill and open its old door and window holes.

name: Hedge House
key_features: Concrete and glass art pavilion in the garden of Kasteel Wijlre, set low between tall hedges.

name: Peckham Library
key_features: Inverted L on thin raking steel legs over a public square; pre-patinated copper skin and coloured glass.

name: Newport Street Gallery
key_features: Listed Victorian workshops joined to new brick end buildings with sawtooth roofs; galleries run through all of them.

name: Everyman Theatre
key_features: Front of metal sunshades cut with life-size portraits of local people; walls of brick reclaimed from the old theatre.

name: Velodrom and Swimming Hall, Berlin
key_features: A round velodrome and a long pool hall sunk into an orchard, only their flat metal-mesh roofs showing.

name: The Neurosciences Institute
key_features: Research buildings arranged as a small 'monastery' around a sunken plaza, with ramps, stairs and outdoor rooms.

name: Moesgaard Museum
key_features: A wedge-shaped museum whose sloping grass roof rises out of the land and doubles as a public hill.

name: Goldsmith Street
key_features: Passivhaus council homes in tight brick terraces, with a shared planted alley between the back gardens.

name: New Library, Magdalene College
key_features: Brick walls and tall chimneys frame timber reading bays lit from pitched glazed roof lanterns.

name: Stormen Concert Hall and Library
key_features: Concert hall with three venues and a library as a pair; the library's reading room looks out to the harbour.

name: The New Art Gallery Walsall
key_features: A tower clad in pale grey terracotta tiles over the canal basin; timber-lined galleries with carefully varied daylight.

name: Lewis Glucksman Gallery
key_features: Timber-clad gallery volumes lifted on slim columns above a limestone plinth, among trees on the university grounds.

name: Weald and Downland Gridshell
key_features: Three-domed lattice of thin green oak laths, shaped like a peanut shell, over a sunken artefact store.

name: Hall of Nations
key_features: Truncated pyramid of reinforced-concrete space frame, the first of its span in concrete; demolished 2017.

name: Shri Ram Centre for Performing Arts
key_features: Raw-concrete theatre whose auditorium is a heavy box lifted over the street corner.

name: India International Centre
key_features: Low wings by Lodhi Gardens with stone walls, jali screens and thin concrete shades: Stein's 'Steinabad' start.

name: Masjid-e-Tooba
by: Babar Hameed Chauhan, Zaheer Haider Naqvi
key_features: One 65 m column-free dome resting on a low ring wall, with a single 37 m minaret, faced in white marble.

name: Teacher-Student Centre, University of Dhaka
key_features: Student centre around a courtyard, its main block under a double 'butterfly' roof that shades and cools.

name: Makoko Floating School
key_features: 10 m timber A-frame on about 250 plastic barrels: play deck, louvred classrooms, open-air classroom on top.

name: Royal Theatre of Rabat
key_features: Sweeping curved shell on the Bou Regreg riverbank, with a muqarnas-faceted 1,821-seat hall and outdoor amphitheatre.

name: Nid d'Abeille, Carrières Centrales
key_features: The patio house stacked five levels high: private open-air patios staggered floor by floor into a honeycomb facade.

name: Krushi Bhawan
key_features: Government office wrapped in a brick screen patterned after Odisha ikat, in three local clays, around public gardens.

name: Gaddafi Stadium
by: Nasreddin Murat-Khan; Nayyar Ali Dada (1996 redesign)
key_features: Cricket ground re-clad by Nayyar Ali Dada in hand-laid red brick and arches, with shops under the stands.

name: Highpoint I
key_features: 64 flats in white reinforced concrete on a double-cross plan, engineered by Ove Arup; Grade I listed.

name: Penguin Pool, London Zoo
key_features: Two interlocking spiral ramps of thin reinforced concrete cross an elliptical pool.

name: St Peter's Seminary
by: Gillespie, Kidd & Coia (Isi Metzstein, Andy MacMillan)
key_features: Terraces of student rooms stack over the chapel and refectory; closed 1980, abandoned since 1987.

name: Royal Commonwealth Pool
by: Robert Matthew, Johnson-Marshall and Partners (John Richards)
key_features: Built for the 1970 Commonwealth Games: long, low modernist pool halls, with Ove Arup as engineer.

name: Sonneveld House
key_features: Nieuwe Bouwen villa of steel and glass, kept with its original interior as a museum house.

name: Schocken Department Store, Chemnitz
key_features: Arched street front of horizontal window strips; now the State Museum of Archaeology (smac).

name: Hotel Avion
key_features: Hotel on a medieval plot about 8 m wide: galleried café floors at shifting levels behind a glazed front.

name: Villa Stiassni
key_features: Functionalist villa for textile industrialist Alfred Stiassni, set in a large terraced garden above Brno.

name: Prudential House
by: Marcin Weinfeld; steel frame by Stefan Bryła and Wenczesław Poniż
key_features: 66 m steel-framed tower whose frame survived the shelling of the 1944 Warsaw Uprising; now a hotel.

name: Kaunas Central Post Office
key_features: Interwar post office of the temporary capital, a key work of UNESCO-listed Modernist Kaunas.

name: Resurrection Chapel
key_features: Asymmetric barrel-vaulted chapel whose glazed aisle opens along its length to the cemetery woods.

name: Turun Sanomat Building
key_features: The first building in Turku with strip windows: a Corbusian concrete frame, slabs on pillars, presses below.

name: Sunila Pulp Mill and Housing
key_features: Aalto's pulp mill, workers' housing and town plan for Ahlström, built 1937-39.

name: Sanatorium Joseph Lemaire
key_features: Modernist tuberculosis sanatorium by Maxime Brunfaut at Overijse, near Brussels.
